title: Prospectivity Lens: Deployment Friction Mosaic & Buyer Propensity Fieldbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a repeatable 'Prospectivity Lens' artifact that scores models and vendors by (a) buyer propensity for adoption and (b) deployment friction for Redwood customers. The deliverable is a mosaic report + a lightweight dashboard that surfaces priority signals for Product, Sales, and GTM.

Why now: rapid new open model flavors and region-specific availability shifts are increasing procurement friction. PM needs a way to prioritize model onboarding and fallback investments by expected buyer demand and real engineering lift.

Scope and outputs:
- Fieldbook (PDF/Confluence): definition of metrics, signal sources, weighting guidance, and recommended actions for top-10 model-vendor combos.
- Prospectivity Score: a combined numerical score (0-100) per model variant.
- Deployment Friction Mosaic: a categorical heatmap (regions × friction buckets) covering quantization fit, licensing constraints, infra affinity, latency footprint, and support maturity.
- Dashboard prototype: lightweight Looker/Metabase dashboard surfaced in Console backlog for stakeholders.

Signal sources (examples):
- Internal telemetry: P50/P95 latency by region, paging rates, cache hit ratio, token cost per 1k, failed deployment attempts.
- Onboarding notes: infra pre-reqs (CUDA/CUDNN, unsupported ops), quantization issues, required kernel patches.
- Commercial signals: license restrictions (non-commercial, research-only), vendor SLA, procurement lead time.
- Market signals: open-source repo activity, upstream model version cadence, provider outage history.
- Sales funnel signals: inbound RFP counts mentioning model, prospect vertical, expected latency constraint.

Methodology (high-level):
1) Define friction dimensions (technical, contractual, regional) and buyer propensity dimensions (vertical fit, buyer size, latency sensitivity, cost sensitivity).
2) Normalize each signal to 0-10, with documented normalization functions stored in the Fieldbook.
3) Combine into two sub-scores: PropensityScore and FrictionScore. Compute Prospectivity = PropensityScore * (1 - FrictionScoreWeight). Tunable weight parameter in config.
4) Rank models and produce top-N candidate list per vertical and region.

Success criteria:
- Fieldbook finished and reviewed by PM/Eng/SEs by 2026-03-24.
- Dashboard prototype shows top-20 model-variants across three regions with Prospectivity and friction dimensions by 2026-03-31.
- Feedback loop established with Sales (weekly signal digest) and Model Ops (deployment telemetry mapping).

Runbook actions (if Prospectivity drops sharply):
- Trigger model-onboarding task: open ENG ticket to investigate quantization/kernel gaps.
- Trigger commercial follow-up: Sales/BD to clarify licensing or vendor timelines.
- Mark for Dedicated capacity pilot if regional latency is a blocker.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Weight tuning: how aggressively should friction penalize promising models? (initial default: 40% friction weight).
- Data freshness: Sales signals are low-frequency; to avoid stale scores we will age commercial signals after 30 days.
- Coverage vs fidelity: prioritize breadth of models for initial rollout; increase fidelity for top-10.

Next steps (first two sprints):
- Sprint 1 (Mar 10–Mar 24): finalize signal definitions, build normalization helpers, draft Fieldbook, prototype dashboard skeleton.
- Sprint 2 (Mar 25–Apr 07): wire telemetry sources, validate against 3 historical model onboarding cases, stakeholder review, iterate on weights.
